verified_scope_note: Verified for personal, non-commercial travel from the United States to Canada (dogs and cats).

requirements.title: Microchip recorded
requirements.description: A microchip is recommended but NOT required by CFIA for a personal pet entering Canada.

requirements.title: Rabies vaccination valid (certificate in English or French)
requirements.description: A rabies vaccination is required for animals 3 months and older, on a vet certificate in English or French — no APHIS endorsement is needed for Canada.

manual_checklist.title: Confirm this is a non-commercial, privately owned pet movement
manual_checklist.detail: Age, accompaniment, number of dogs, purpose, and ownership-transfer status can change the applicable requirements. Commercial imports (sale, adoption, breeding, retail; ownership transfer) and unaccompanied/multi-dog movements trigger CFIA permits, age minimums, and additional paperwork. Dogs over 8 months generally use the rabies-certificate route.

manual_checklist.title: Health certificate may be required: unaccompanied or 3+ dogs 8 months old or younger
manual_checklist.detail: CFIA's rabies-certificate-only route (no separate health certificate) applies when your dog is: older than 8 months (regardless of accompaniment or count); OR, for a dog 8 months old or younger, one of 2 or fewer such dogs travelling WITH their owner; OR a certified guide, hearing, or service dog accompanying its handler; OR temporarily exported for a competition or trial. Outside those categories — an UNACCOMPANIED dog 8 months old or younger, or 3 or more dogs 8 months old or younger travelling together — CFIA requires a health certificate that Petra does not check for. Confirm your movement fits one of the qualifying categories; if not, arrange the health certificate separately.

manual_checklist.title: Confirm this is a domestic cat (or an F5+ generation hybrid)
manual_checklist.detail: CFIA's personal cat route covers only domestic cats (Felis catus) and F5-or-later generation hybrids. Non-domestic cats and early-generation (F1 to F4) hybrids need a CFIA import permit and are NOT covered by this verified route. Confirm your cat is a domestic cat or an F5+ hybrid before relying on the rabies-certificate route.

manual_checklist.title: Rabies certificate in English or French, identifying the animal
manual_checklist.detail: Present an acceptable rabies certificate — in English OR French (not necessarily both), issued and signed by a licensed vet, clearly identifying the animal (breed, colour, weight) and showing a current rabies vaccination. It does NOT need APHIS endorsement for Canada.

manual_checklist.title: Why rabies isn't being requested: pet is under 3 months
manual_checklist.detail: This pet is under 3 months old, so CFIA does not require a rabies record and Petra has skipped that check. Carry ordinary evidence of the animal's age (the rabies certificate is not the only acceptable age record). (This note only appears for under-90-day pets.)

manual_checklist.title: Proof of the kitten's age (under 3 months)
manual_checklist.detail: This cat is under 3 months old and rabies-exempt, but CFIA requires proof of the cat's age at the border. Carry documentary evidence of the kitten's age (the rabies certificate is not the only acceptable age record) and confirm you have it.

manual_checklist.title: Present the pet to a CBSA officer on arrival
manual_checklist.detail: At the border, present the pet and its rabies certificate to a CBSA officer for a document check + visual inspection.

supporting_requirements: no import permit / endorsed health cert for the personal route
